children: Shares of Weatherford International climbed after the global energy services company forecasted its Venezuela revenue to ramp up to triple-digits in 2027.
The stock ticked up 7% to $84.69 on Wednesday. The shares are up 8.3% year-to-date.

Chief Executive Girish Saligram said on the earnings call Weatherford expects to see further increases in Venezuela in 2028, with potential for the company to reach its prior peak in the next few years. Weatherford also expects to see tangible revenue contribution from Venezuela in the fourth quarter.

The company after the close on Tuesday posted a profit of $120 million, or $1.66 a share, compared with $81 million, or $1.12 a share, in the third quarter. Analysts polled by FactSet expected $1.33 a share.
Revenue was $1.14 billion, beating Wall Street analyst expectations of $1.13 billion.
The company's portfolio is levered to upcoming developments in 2027, including a reopening in Venezuela and a stabilizing Mexico, according to Melius Research analysts.
Even as conflict-related operational disruptions in the Middle East weighed on activity levels, the readouts reiterated the durability of the company's operating model, Saligram said.
